incidents.cause: The loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined based on the available information.
A partial loss of engine power for undetermined reasons.
The inability of either pilot to see the other airplane due to the blind spot created by their respective airplane's wings.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing rollout, resulting in a ground loop and runway excursion.
The loss of engine power due to the separation of the No. 2 cylinder exhaust rocker boss housing, which prevented the exhaust valve from opening.

The pilot’s failure to maintain adequate clearance from an object during an aerial application, which resulted in damage to the landing gear and led to the airplane ground looping during the subsequent landing.
The pilot's decision to land on an unsuitable landing surface into bright sunlight, which resulted in a loss of control.
The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack for unknown reason, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and a loss of control.

The pilot's improper landing flare, which resulted in a bounced landing, and his subsequent failure to maintain directional control during landing with a gusting crosswind, which resulted in a ground-loop.
The failure of the right main landing gearbox assembly due to fatigue cracking, which resulted in a loss of directional control during the landing roll.
The pilot’s loss of directional control during landing, which resulted in a ground loop.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll.
